title: Stage 2: Encrypted entries
summary: Store secrets with AES-GCM, take nonces from a counter that never repeats, bind each ciphertext to its name, and catch tampering.

steps.title: Stage 2: secrets go in
body: Now the vault stores secrets. Each entry is sealed with **AES-GCM** under the master key:
| `put <name> <secret...>` | `stored <name> (<ciphertext length> bytes)`; the secret may contain spaces; an existing name is replaced |
| `list` | `entries: a, b, c` (ordinal order) or `entries: (none)`; works while locked |
| `tamper <name>` | `tampered <name>`, after flipping the lowest bit of ciphertext byte 0 (`Cipher[0] ^= 1`) |
| `swap <a> <b>` | `swapped <a> <b>`, after exchanging the two stored entries |
- **Nonce:** 12 bytes, 4 zero bytes then a 64-bit **big-endian counter**. The counter starts at 0 and is incremented *before* each use, so the first nonce is `000000000000000000000001`.
- **Associated data:** the UTF-8 entry name. It is not encrypted, but the tag covers it.

Errors: `put` or `get` while locked (or before `init`): `error: locked`; a missing name or secret: `error: missing argument`; an unknown name for `get`, `dump`, `tamper` or `swap`: `error: no entry <name>` (for `swap`, check `a` first); a failed tag check: `error: <name> has been tampered with`. Everything from stage 1 must keep working.

steps.explain: Big-endian writes the most significant byte first, so 258 (0x0102) ends in `0102`. 64 bits of counter will not run out: at a billion encryptions a second that is over 500 years.

steps.title: Why a counter, and why it is fine here
body: AES-GCM's one hard rule: **never encrypt two messages with the same key and nonce.** Reuse leaks the XOR of the plaintexts and lets an attacker forge tags (module 3).
There are two safe ways to pick nonces:
- **Random** 12-byte nonces from `RandomNumberGenerator`. Simple and what most code should do, but with random 96-bit nonces you should stop at about 2^32 messages per key.

- A **counter** that is stored and never goes backwards. Deterministic, which makes these tests possible and makes reuse impossible *as long as the counter is never reset or forked*. In stage 5 you will meet the trap: restoring an old backup can rewind it.
Step through the counter below: the state that matters is the single `counter` variable, and every nonce is derived from it.

steps.prompt: Why does the vault pass the entry *name* as associated data?
options: So a ciphertext moved to a different name (a swap) fails to decrypt instead of returning the wrong secret
steps.explain: Without it, an attacker who can edit the vault file could swap your `bank` and `github` entries and you would paste the wrong password into the wrong site. Associated data binds the ciphertext to its context.
GCM's ciphertext is exactly as long as the plaintext; the 16-byte tag is separate. The associated data is the name.

steps.title: Seal and open entries
prompt: Add `put`, `get`, `list`, `dump`, `tamper` and `swap` as specified. Store each entry as a `record Entry(byte[] Nonce, byte[] Cipher, byte[] Tag)` in a `Dictionary<string, Entry>` (ordinal).
error: github has been tampered with
`dump` is exact: it only matches if your key, nonce layout, associated data and tag size all follow the spec. Catch `AuthenticationTagMismatchException` to report tampering.
starter: // Tests only: a real vault uses 600,000+ iterations and a random salt stored next to the vault.
byte[]? keyCheck;    // stored with the vault: proves a password is right without storing the key
byte[]? masterKey;   // only in memory, only while unlocked
string Arg(int i) => i < parts.Length ? parts[i] : "";
"status" => keyCheck is null ? "no vault" : masterKey is null ? "locked" : "unlocked",
static byte[] KeyCheck(byte[] key) => HMACSHA256.HashData(key, Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("key-check"));
if (keyCheck is not null) return "error: vault already exists";
if (keyCheck is null) return "error: no vault";
if (keyCheck is null) return "error: no vault";
solution: // Tests only: a real vault uses 600,000+ iterations and a random salt stored next to the vault.
byte[]? keyCheck;    // stored with the vault: proves a password is right without storing the key
byte[]? masterKey;   // only in memory, only while unlocked
ulong counter;       // last nonce used under the master key; never goes backwards
string Arg(int i) => i < parts.Length ? parts[i] : "";
"status" => keyCheck is null ? "no vault" : masterKey is null ? "locked" : "unlocked",
static byte[] KeyCheck(byte[] key) => HMACSHA256.HashData(key, Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("key-check"));
if (keyCheck is not null) return "error: vault already exists";
if (keyCheck is null) return "error: no vault";
if (keyCheck is null) return "error: no vault";
var nonce = new byte[12];                                  // 4 zero bytes, then the counter
// AES-GCM in one place. Open returns null when the tag does not verify.
static (byte[] Cipher, byte[] Tag) Seal(byte[] key, byte[] nonce, byte[] plain, string aad)
static byte[]? Open(byte[] key, byte[] nonce, byte[] cipher, byte[] tag, string aad)
var (cipher, tag) = Seal(masterKey, nonce, Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(secret), name);
if (!entries.TryGetValue(name, out var e)) return $"error: no entry {name}";
var plain = Open(masterKey, e.Nonce, e.Cipher, e.Tag, name);
return plain is null ? $"error: {name} has been tampered with" : $"{name}: {Encoding.UTF8.GetString(plain)}";
if (!entries.TryGetValue(name, out var e)) return $"error: no entry {name}";
e.Cipher[0] ^= 1;                                          // an attacker flips one bit on disk
record Entry(byte[] Nonce, byte[] Cipher, byte[] Tag);

tests.name: put, get and list
tests.stdin:
init correct-horse
put github ghp_secret123
put email hunter2 with spaces
get github
get email
list

tests.name: dump shows the counter nonce, ciphertext and tag
tests.stdin:
init correct-horse
put github ghp_secret123
put email hunter2
dump github
dump email

tests.name: a locked vault refuses put and get
tests.stdin:
put early bird
init correct-horse
put a one
lock
get a
put b two
list
unlock correct-horse
get a

tests.name: a flipped bit is detected
tests.stdin:
init correct-horse
put github ghp_secret123
tamper github
get github
put github ghp_new456
get github
expect: error: github has been tampered with

tests.name: swapped entries are detected
tests.stdin:
init correct-horse
put a one
put b two
swap a b
get a
get b
expect: error: a has been tampered with
error: b has been tampered with

tests.name: missing entries and an empty list
tests.stdin:
init correct-horse
list
get nope
tamper nope
dump nope
swap nope other

tests.name: lock, a wrong password, then the right one
tests.stdin:
init correct-horse
lock
status
unlock wrong-horse
status
unlock correct-horse
status

hints: Write `Seal(key, nonce, plain, aad)` and `Open(...)` helpers once; stage 3 will use them for two different keys.
Split with `line.Split(' ', 3, ...)` (already in the starter) so the third part keeps its spaces.
